Rashi on Yevamot 50a:1:1.english: Years of generations - Years that are allotted to a person at the time of his birth.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:1:2.english: [If] he is deserving, they add to his [lifespan] - And this "I will fulfill" [in the verse] is an expression of addition.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:2:1.english: From his own they added to him - Rather, originally they wanted to subtract from his years.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:2:2.hebrew: תדע - שמתחלה כשנולד, נפסקו לו כל אותו תוספת:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:2:2.english: Know - For from the beginning, when [Hezekiah] was born, that entire addition was allotted to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:2:3.hebrew: שהרי נביא נתנבא - בימי ירבעם, שנים הרבה קודם: ״הנה בן נולד לבית דוד יאשיהו שמו״. ובשעת חליו של חזקיה עדיין לא נולד מנשה, שממנו יצא יאשיהו. הוי אומר: בשעת חליו גזרו לפחות משניו, וכשזכה השלימו לו:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:2:3.english: As a prophet prophesied - in the days of Jeroboam, many years earlier: "Behold, a son shall be born to the House of David, Josiah is his name." And at the time of Hezekiah's illness, Manasseh, from whom Josiah descended, had not yet been born. Thus you must say: at the time of his illness they decreed to subtract from his years, and when he merited [it], they completed [them] for him.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:4:1.hebrew: משנה שאינה צריכה - דזיל קרי בי רב הוא, "עליה בחייה", שלא נאסרה אחותה אלא בחייה:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:4:1.english: An unnecessary mishna - For it is [a matter of] "go read in the schoolhouse" [i.e., an explicit verse]: "besides her, in her lifetime" [Leviticus 18:18], [teaching] that her sister is forbidden only during her lifetime.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:2.hebrew: רבן גמליאל אומר - סדר משנה זו, שלא תטעה לשבש הגירסא שבספרים. סדר יבם אחד ויבמה אחת — תחלה מפרש דין גט וחליצה וביאה שאחר מאמר, ואח"כ מפרש דין מאמר וביאה וחליצה שאחר הגט, ואח"כ דין מאמר וגט וביאה שאחר החליצה, ואח"כ דין מאמר וגט וחליצה שאחר הביאה. וכן סדר יבם א' ושתי יבמות:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:2.english: Rabban Gamliel says - [Here is] the order of this Mishnah, so that you do not err [and come] to corrupt the text in the books. [First is] the order of one yavam and one yevama — first it explains the law of a bill of divorce [get], ḥalitza, and intercourse after levirate betrothal [ma'amar]; and afterward it explains the law of levirate betrothal, intercourse, and ḥalitza after a bill of divorce; and afterward the law of levirate betrothal, a bill of divorce, and intercourse after ḥalitza; and afterward the law of levirate betrothal, a bill of divorce, and ḥalitza after intercourse. And similarly [is] the order of one yavam and two yevamot.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:3.hebrew: אין גט אחר גט - שתי יבמות לאדם אחד מאח אחד, ונתן גט לזו וגט לזו, אינו אסור בקרובות שניה, דאי קמא אהני, הא פקעה זיקה דתרוייהו והוי כמגרש נכרית; ואי קמא לא אהני למידחי, בתרא נמי לא אהני, והלכך לאו גרושתו היא. וכן שני יבמין ליבמה אחת, ונתן זה גט וזה גט, האחרון אינו כלום ומותר בקרובותיה, וטעמא כדפרישית:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:3.english: There is no bill of divorce after a bill of divorce - [If] one man has two yevamot from one brother, and he gave a bill of divorce [get] to this one and a get to that one, he is not forbidden to [marry] the relatives of the second [woman]. For if the first [get] was effective, the levirate bond of both of them has dissolved, and it is like divorcing an unrelated woman; and if the first was not effective to reject [her], the latter is also not effective, and therefore she is not his divorcee. And similarly, [if there are] two brothers-in-law [yevamin] for one yevama, and this one gave a get and that one gave a get, the latter [get] is nothing and he is permitted to [marry] her relatives, and the reason is as I explained.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:4.hebrew: ולא מאמר אחר מאמר - בין ביבם אחד לשתי יבמות, בין שני יבמים ליבמה אחת, האחרון אין כלום לפסול את הראשונה עליו, ואינה צריכה הימנו גט, ולא ליאסר בקרובות השניה:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:4.english: And no levirate betrothal [ma'amar] after levirate betrothal - Whether with one yavam to two yevamot [or] two yevamim to one yevama, the latter [ma'amar] is nothing — [neither] to disqualify the first [yevama] to him, and she does not require a bill of divorce [get] from him, nor to become forbidden to the relatives of the second [yevama].

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:5.hebrew: ולא בעילה אחר בעילה - בא על זו וחזר ובא הוא או אחיו על צרתה, ביאת זנות בעלמא הוא, ואין אסור בקרובותיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:5.english: And [there is] no intercourse after intercourse - [If] he had intercourse with this [woman] and then he or his brother had intercourse with her rival wife, it is merely an act of licentious intercourse, and he is not forbidden to [marry] her relatives.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:6.hebrew: יש גט אחר גט - דקמא לא דחה לגמרי, הלכך אכתי איכא פלגא זיקה, דהא בעיא חליצה. הלכך אהני בתרא, והויא גרושתו ואסור בקרובותיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:6:6.english: A bill of divorce is [effective] after a bill of divorce - For the first [bill of divorce] did not completely push [her] away, therefore half a levirate bond still remains, since she [still] requires ḥalitza. Therefore the latter [bill of divorce] takes effect, and she becomes his divorcee and he is forbidden [to marry] her relatives.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:1.hebrew: כיצד - לאו אפלוגתא קאי, אלא מלתא באנפי נפשה היא, ואיבם אחד ואיבמה אחת קאי. והכי קאמר: כיצד דין יבם ויבמה? והכי מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:1.english: How - It does not refer to the dispute; rather, it is an independent matter, and it refers to one yavam and one yevama. And this is what it is saying: What is the law of a yavam and a yevama? And so it is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:2.hebrew: צריכה הימנו חליצה - ואם רצה לכנוס לא יכנוס, דכיון דהתחיל בגירושין, קיימא עליה ב"לא יבנה":
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:2.english: She requires ḥalitza from him - And if he wishes to take [her] in marriage, he may not take [her] in marriage, for since he began with divorce, she is subject for him to [the prohibition of] "he shall not build" [Deuteronomy 25:9].

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:3.hebrew: צריכה הימנו גט - דחליצה אפקעתה לזיקתה, ובעי גט לאפקועי קדושין דיליה, דחליצה לא מפקעת קידושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:3.english: She requires a bill of divorce from him - For ḥalitza removed her levirate bond, and she requires a bill of divorce to remove his betrothal, as ḥalitza does not remove betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:7:4.english: This is in accordance with its mitzva - The Gemara explains: This too is in accordance with its mitzva.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:1.hebrew: נתן גט ועשה מאמר - באותה יבמה עצמה, אפי' ר"ג מודה דיש מאמר אחר הגט, דמספקא ליה אי גט דחי אי לא, ודלמא גט לא דחי ואהני מאמר יבמין בה. וכ"ש לרבנן דאמרי גט דוחה קצת ומשייר קצת, אהני מאמר למיקני שיורא דגט, וצריך גט למאמרו וחליצה לזיקתו, ויבומי לא, דמגט קמא קיימא עליה בלא יבנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:1.english: [If] he gave a bill of divorce and performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal] - With that same yevamah herself, even Rabban Gamliel agrees that ma'amar takes effect after a bill of divorce, for he is uncertain whether a bill of divorce pushes away [the levirate bond] or not, and perhaps a bill of divorce does not push [it] away, so levirate ma'amar takes effect on her. And all the more so according to the Rabbis, who say [that] a bill of divorce pushes away slightly and leaves a remainder slightly, ma'amar takes effect to acquire the remainder [left by] the bill of divorce; and he requires a bill of divorce for his ma'amar and ḥalitza for his levirate bond, but [he may] not [perform] yibbum [levirate marriage], because from the first bill of divorce she stands [forbidden] to him under [the prohibition of] "he shall not build."

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:2.hebrew: נתן גט ובעל - אסור לקיימה, דקמה עליה ב"לא יבנה", וצריכה גט לביאתו וחליצה לזיקתו. גט לביאתו — ואפילו לר' עקיבא דאמר אין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין, דהא הך מתני' כולה ר' עקיבא היא כדמפרש בגמ' — הכא מודי דתפסי קידושי ביאה, דגט לאו כחליצה דמי לאפקועי כולה זיקה, הלכך לא עמדה עליו בלאו גמור:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:2.english: [If] he gave a bill of divorce and engaged in intercourse - It is forbidden for him to keep her [as a wife], since she stands [forbidden] to him under [the prohibition of] "he shall not build," and she requires a bill of divorce for his intercourse and ḥalitza for his levirate bond. A bill of divorce for his intercourse — even according to Rabbi Akiva, who says that betrothal does not take effect for those liable for negative prohibitions, for this entire Mishnah follows Rabbi Akiva, as explained in the Gemara — here he concedes that betrothal through intercourse takes effect, because a bill of divorce is not like ḥalitza to remove the entire levirate bond; therefore, she did not stand [forbidden] to him under a complete negative prohibition.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:3.hebrew: וחליצה - לזיקתו. ובגט לחודיה לא מפטרא [כמו] שאחר כונס את יבמתו שיכול לפוטרה בגט, משום דהוי ביאה פסולה משום גט קמא ולא קניא לגמרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:3.english: And ḥalitza - For his levirate bond. And she is not released by a bill of divorce alone, like another [yavam] who marries his yevama, who can release her with a bill of divorce, because it is an invalid intercourse due to the first bill of divorce, and she is not acquired completely.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:4.hebrew: אין לאחר חליצה כלום - ואע"ג דחליצה פסולה היא, דאי הוה בעי לייבומי לא מצי, ואפ"ה דחיא לגמרי ואין אחריה כלום, דאי הדר ומקדש לה במאמר או בביאה לא בעינן גט. וכדרבי עקיבא דאמר: אין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין. והכי מפרש בגמ' דמתני' ר"ע היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:8:4.english: Nothing [is effective] after ḥalitza - Even though it is an invalid ḥalitza — for if he had wanted to perform levirate marriage, he could not [do so] — even so, it dismisses [her] completely, and there is nothing after it; for if he goes back and betroths her through levirate betrothal or through intercourse, we do not require a bill of divorce. And [this is] in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who says: Betrothal does not take effect with [those forbidden by] negative commandments. And so it is explained in the Gemara, that our Mishnah is [the view of] Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:9:1.hebrew: חלץ ועשה בה מאמר - או נתן גט אחר חליצה, או בעל אחר חליצה, אינו כלום, כדתני בסיפא: אין אחר חליצה כלום, שאין מאמר וביאה תופסין בה אחר חליצה, כר' עקיבא. וגט דאחר חליצה לא הוה צריך למיתני לאשמועינן דאין כלום, דלמאי ליהני? ליתסורי בקרובותיה? הא מיתסר וקאי מחמת חליצה! אלא איידי דבעי למיתני גט דאחר בעילה, כדקתני: או בעל ועשה מאמר ונתן גט, לאשמועינן דאין לאחר ביאה כלום זיקת יבומים ובהאי גט סגי ליה בלא חליצה, תנא נמי גט דאחר חליצה, והכי מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:9:1.english: [If] he performed ḥalitza and performed levirate betrothal with her - or gave a bill of divorce after ḥalitza, or engaged in intercourse after ḥalitza, it is nothing, as [the Mishnah] teaches in the latter clause: "There is nothing after ḥalitza," for neither levirate betrothal nor intercourse takes effect on her after ḥalitza, in accordance with Rabbi Akiva. And [regarding] a bill of divorce after ḥalitza, it was not necessary to teach [it] to inform us that it is nothing, for what could it avail? To forbid him to her relatives? He already stands forbidden [to them] on account of ḥalitza! Rather, since [the Tanna] needed to teach a bill of divorce after intercourse — as it teaches: "or engaged in intercourse, and performed levirate betrothal, and gave a bill of divorce" — to inform us that after intercourse there is nothing [remaining] of the levirate bond and with this bill of divorce it suffices for him without ḥalitza, he also taught a bill of divorce after ḥalitza; and so it is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:9:2.hebrew: או בעל ועשה מאמר - או נתן גט אחר ביאה, או חלץ אחר ביאה — אין לאחר ביאה כלום זיקת יבמים, דגט שנתן אחר ביאה מגרש לה כאשתו גמורה, ולא בעיא חליצה, ואם רצה להחזיר — מחזירה. וחליצה שעשה אחר ביאה אינה מועלת כלום, דאין עליה זיקת יבמין. ומאמר דאחר ביאה לא הוה צריך למיתני, דפשיטא לן דלא מהני; דלמאי ליהני? הא אפילו מאמר אחר מאמר ביבם אחד ויבמה אחת, בתרא כמאן דליתיה דמי, דמאי קעביד? הא מיתסר וקאי בקרובותיה. אלא איידי דתנא רישא חלץ ועשה מאמר, דאיצטריך לאשמועינן כר' עקיבא דאין קידושין תופסין בחלוצתו, תנא נמי בעל ועשה מאמר; והכי מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:9:2.english: Or if he engaged in intercourse and performed ma'amar - or gave a bill of divorce after intercourse, or performed chalitzah after intercourse — there is nothing of the levirate bond after intercourse, for a bill of divorce that he gave after intercourse divorces her like his full wife, and she does not require chalitzah, and if he wishes to take [her] back, he may take her back. And a chalitzah that he performed after intercourse is of no avail at all, because there is no levirate bond upon her. Now, [the case of] ma'amar after intercourse did not need to be taught, for it is obvious to us that it is ineffective; for what could it accomplish? Why, even [in the case of] ma'amar after ma'amar with one yavam and one yevamah, the latter [ma'amar] is considered as if it does not exist, for what does it accomplish? Behold, he already stands forbidden to her relatives. Rather, since [the Tanna] taught in the first clause [the case of] "he performed chalitzah and performed ma'amar," which was necessary to teach us in accordance with Rabbi Akiva that betrothal does not take effect with one's chalutzah, he also taught "he engaged in intercourse and performed ma'amar." And so it is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 50a:9:3.hebrew: אין אחר חליצה כלום - ארישא קאי, וכדפרישית לעיל. ואלישנא דסיפא, דקתני "או בעל ועשה מאמר או נתן גט וחלץ", הוה שייך למיתני "אין אחר ביאה כלום", ובגמרא קא בעי ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 50a:9:3.english: There is nothing after ḥalitza - [This] refers to the first clause, as I explained above. And regarding the wording of the latter clause, which teaches, "or he engaged in intercourse and performed levirate betrothal, or gave a bill of divorce and performed ḥalitza," it would have been appropriate to teach, "there is nothing after intercourse," and in the Gemara [it] raises this [question].

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:1:1.hebrew: מוסיפין לו - והא דאמר במועד קטן (דף כח. ושם): "בני חיי ומזוני לאו בזכותא תליא מילתא, אלא במזלא תליא מילתא" — פשיטא דזכות גדול מועיל, כדאמר בשבת (דף קנו: ושם): "אין מזל לישראל". ומיהו לא שכיח שישתנה המזל, כדמוכח בתענית (דף כה.) גבי עובדא דר"א בן פדת:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:1:1.english: They add [years] to his [lifespan] - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in Moed Katan (28a and there): "Children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, rather they depend on [astrological] fortune" — it is obvious that great merit helps, as [the Gemara] says in Shabbat (156b and there): "There is no [astrological] fortune for Israel." However, it is uncommon for [one's] fortune to change, as is evident in Taanit (25a) regarding the incident of Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:2:1.hebrew: משלו הוסיפו לו - וקרי ליה תוספת לפי מה שנגזר לפחות ע"י עון. והא דאמר בפ"ק דחגיגה (דף ד: ושם) גבי איתתא מגדלא נשיא: "כי חזינן צורבא מרבנן דמעבר אמיליה מוסיפין ליה" — אר"י דניחא אפילו לר"ע, דאין זה תוספת כיון שנגזרו לשום אדם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:2:1.english: From his own they added to him - And [Scripture] calls it an "addition" relative to what had been decreed to be reduced on account of sin. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Chagigah (4b, and there) regarding the woman who braided women's hair: "When we see a Torah scholar who foregoes his pride [and overlooks insults], we add [years] to him" — Ri says that this is satisfactory even according to Rabbi Akiva, for this is not an [unallotted] addition, since [those years] had [already] been decreed for some person.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:2:2.hebrew: תדע שהרי נביא עומד - וא"ת: והלא אם לא התפלל חזקיהו על עצמו, היה מת והיתה נבואה בטלה? אלא ע"כ, אין הנביא מתנבא אלא מה שראוי להיות אם לא היה חוטא; א"כ, היכי מוכח מכאן דמשלו הוסיפו לו? אפי' לא הוסיפו לו משלו, וחיה כבר כל שנותיו שנגזרו לו, מה שלא נתקיימה הנבואה לפי שחטא, ואילו לא חטא ונשא אשה בשנים הראשונים, היה מוליד. ואר"י, דשמא הדורות נגזרו להוולד באותו הזמן ובאותו הפרק שהם נולדים, ובשני התוספת נגזר לו להוליד מנשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:2:2.english: "Know, as a prophet stood" - And if you will say: Had Hezekiah not prayed for himself, would he not have died and the prophecy have been nullified? Rather, perforce, the prophet only prophesies what is fitting to happen had he not sinned; if so, how is it proven from here that they added to him from his own [allotted years]? Even if they did not add to him from his own, and he had already lived all his years that were decreed for him, [the reason] that the prophecy was not fulfilled [would be] because he sinned, and had he not sinned and [instead] married a wife in [his] earlier years, he would have fathered [children]. And Rabbi Yitzchak says: Perhaps the generations are decreed to be born at the [specific] time and in the [specific] period in which they are born, and [therefore] in the additional years it was decreed for him to father Manasseh.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:4:1.hebrew: שנה רבי משנה שאינה צריכה - פ"ה דזיל קרי בי רב הוא. וקשה, דבכמה מקומות שונה התנא מה שבפסוק בפירוש. ועוד, דגרשה ומתה מותר באחותה — איצטריך למידק הא לא מתה אסירא, דלא כתיב בהדיא, ודרשינן לה בפ"ק (דף ח:) מ"עליה" — בחייה, כל שבחייה, אפילו נתגרשה. אלא נראה לר"י, דיבמתו היא משנה שאין צריכה, דכיון דתנא אשתו — כ"ש יבמתו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:4:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] taught an unnecessary mishna - Rashi explains that it is [a matter of] "go read in the house of the teacher" [i.e., an elementary biblical verse]. And this is difficult, for in several places the Tanna teaches what is explicitly in the verse. And furthermore, regarding [the ruling that if] he divorced her and she died he is permitted to her sister — it was necessary to infer [from this] that if she did not die she is forbidden, for [this] is not written explicitly, and we expound it in the first chapter (8b) from [the word] "aleha" [meaning] during her lifetime — any [time] that is during her lifetime, even if she was divorced. Rather, it appears to the Ri that [the clause of] his yevama is the unnecessary mishna, for once [the Tanna] taught [the case of] his wife, all the more so [is it true of] his yevama.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:6:2.hebrew: רבן גמליאל. אין מאמר אחר מאמר - אתי אפי' כרבנן דרבי עקיבא; אע"ג דקידושין לדידהו תופסין בחייבי לאוין ותפסי קידושין אחר ביאה, התם הוא משום דהוו קדושין דאורייתא, דע"י ביאה פקעה זיקה, אבל הכא שהיא זקוקה לו אין לו לתפוס אלא מדרבנן, ולא תקון רבנן שיהא מאמר אחר מאמר. ולהכי לא קאמר בגמרא עלה: "זו דברי ר' עקיבא", ולא כמו שפי' ריב"ן דר"ג כר"ע:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:6:2.english: Rabban Gamliel [says]: There is no ma'amar after ma'amar - [This] follows even [the view of] the Rabbis who dispute Rabbi Akiva; even though according to them, betrothal [kiddushin] takes effect on those prohibited by a negative commandment and betrothal takes effect after intercourse, there it is because it is a biblical betrothal, since through intercourse the levirate bond [zikah] has been dissolved, whereas here, where she is bound to him by the levirate bond, it [ma'amar] should take effect only by rabbinic decree, and the Rabbis did not institute that there should be ma'amar after ma'amar. Therefore, the Gemara does not say regarding it, "This is the view of Rabbi Akiva," [and it is] not as Rivan explained, that Rabban Gamliel holds like Rabbi Akiva.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:6:3.hebrew: ולא בעילה אחר בעילה - היינו אחר בעילה כשרה, אבל אחר בעילה פסולה — כגון ביאה שאחר הגט — יש אחריה ביאה, כי היכי דיש אחריה מאמר, כמו שאפרש בגמ':
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:6:3.english: Nor intercourse after intercourse - This means after a valid intercourse; however, after an invalid intercourse — such as intercourse that [takes place] after a get — there is [effective] intercourse after it, just as there is [effective] ma'amar after it, as I will explain in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:6:4.english: And [there is] no ḥalitza after ḥalitza - This means even after an invalid ḥalitza.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:7:1.hebrew: עשה מאמר ביבמתו ונתן לה גט צריכה חליצה - היינו בנתן גט סתם, אף לזיקתו; אבל אם נתן גט למאמרו, שריא אף ליבם, דאמר בפ' ד' אחין (לעיל יבמות דף לב.) דהותרה אפי' היא, דמאי דעבד שקליה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:7:1.english: If he performed ma'amar with his yevamah and gave her a bill of divorce, she requires chalitzah - This is [specifically] where he gave an unspecified bill of divorce, [applying] also to his levirate bond. However, if he gave a bill of divorce [specifically] for his ma'amar, she is permitted even to the yavam, as it states in the chapter Arba'ah Achim (above, Yevamot 32a) that even she is permitted, because what he did, he took back.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:7:2.hebrew: עשה מאמר וחלץ צריכה הימנו גט - הכא לא תני "אין אחר חליצה כלום", משום דאכתי צריכה גט למאמר שכבר; ולא תני ליה אלא היכא דאחר חליצה אין צריך לעשות כלום:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:7:2.english: If he performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal] and ḥalitza, she requires a bill of divorce from him - Here [the Mishnah] does not teach "there is nothing after ḥalitza," because she still requires a bill of divorce for the ma'amar that [was] already [performed]; and it only teaches it where, after ḥalitza, there is no need to do anything.

Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:9:1.hebrew: חלץ ועשה מאמר כו' - אומר ריב"ן: לא הוה צריך למיתני כלל, דכיון דתנא "נתן גט וחלץ אין אחר חליצה כלום" אע"פ שהיא חליצה פסולה, כ"ש דאחר חליצה כשירה אין אחריה כלום; אלא כל העניינים שונה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 50a:9:1.english: If he performed ḥalitza and performed levirate betrothal, etc. - Rivan says: It was not necessary to teach [this] at all, for since [the Mishnah] taught [that if] "he gave a bill of divorce and performed ḥalitza, nothing is [effective] after ḥalitza," even though it is an invalid ḥalitza, all the more so that after a valid ḥalitza nothing is [effective] after it; rather, [the Mishnah] teaches all the cases.
